memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After Jacob returned from Paddan Aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him. God said to him, 'Your name is Jacob, but you will no longer be called Jacob; your name will be Israel.' So he named him Israel. And God said to him, 'I am God Almighty; be fruitful and increase in number. A nation and a community of nations will come from you, and kings will come from your body. The land I gave to Abraham and Isaac I also give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you.' Then God went up from him at the place where he had talked with him." - Gen 35:9-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At Bethel, God appears to Jacob again and renews everything. He confirms the new name given at Peniel — "your name will be Israel" — and reaffirms the great covenant promises: fruitfulness, a nation, a community of peoples, and a land. God introduces Himself as "God Almighty" (El Shaddai), the all-powerful One who is more than able to fulfil every word He speaks.

Notice one striking phrase: "kings will come from your body." This was a promise reaching far into the future. From Jacob's line would come King David, and in time the greatest King of all — Jesus Christ, the King of kings, born of this very family (Rev 19:16; Luke 1:32-33). At Bethel, God was pointing forward to the coming of His Son.

Notice too the timing of this renewal. God confirms His promises right after Jacob has obeyed, buried the idols, and returned to Him. When we come back to God wholeheartedly, He loves to reaffirm His purposes for us. Returning to God is never a step backward; it opens the way for Him to renew His promises in our lives.

Whatever God has promised you in His Word, He is "God Almighty" — fully able to bring it to pass. His covenant faithfulness does not fail. Draw near to Him, and let Him renew your confidence in His unchanging promises.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God is "Almighty" — fully able to keep His promises?
2. How does it move me that the King, Jesus, came from this promise?
3. Where do I need God to renew my confidence in His Word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Almighty God, thank You for Your unfailing promises, fulfilled in Christ the King. As I return to You, renew my confidence in Your Word, and help me to trust that You are able to do all You have said. Amen.
